full_judgment: 50. From a bare reading, we do not find any scope of its application in a property owned by the government inasmuch as no one can be allowed to pretend to be the owner of a government owned property and, as such, the concept of the "ostensible owner" is not applicable where the dispute is with regard to "Khas land" and "acquired land". Further, the word "person" used therein does not denote the government inasmuch as from the definition clauses of the General Clauses Act, it does not appear that government is meant to be a "person".
